Ahmedabad, India — Selected work

Anyone can make one good shot. I make sixteen.

Generative video is easy once. It's hard consistently — and consistency is the only thing that turns clips into a commercial. Here's what I've made, and how.

01 — The problem

Most AI ads die at scene three.

Every generation is a fresh roll of the dice. The model has no memory of the shot before it, so by the third clip the face has shifted, the product has changed proportions, and the light has jumped from window-left to window-right.

You notice it even if you can't name it. The ad stops feeling like a film and starts feeling like a folder of clips — and the viewer's trust in the product goes with it.

Scene 01 — kitchen counter, morning key

02 — The method

So I write the film before I generate it.

A style bible fixes the rules once — lighting direction, colour ratio, lens character — and every shot inherits them instead of inventing its own.

Continuity anchors describe the character and the product in language precise enough that scene sixteen still matches scene one.

Shot-by-shot direction gives each scene a lens, a camera move and blocking, so generation has something to obey rather than something to guess.

Scene 06 — interior, follow, 35mm

03 — Raza Communications

One day, one look, sixteen scenes.

Wireless headphones and a power bank carried through a single story — kitchen counter, hallway, street, office. Same character, same products, same light discipline from first frame to last.

04 — Product film

Studio light, no studio.

Lit the way a real product table would be: key from the left, a rim tracing the edge, charge indicator staying legible right through the rotation.

The turn is slow on purpose. Fast rotation hides build quality; slow rotation sells it.

Format9:16 vertical
ToolSeedance 2.0

05 — Product film

Motion that points at the product.

Light trails wrap the headset and settle on the control face — so the eye lands exactly where the buying decision gets made.

That path is choreographed in the shotlist, not hoped for in the prompt. It's the difference between a flourish and a sales tool.

Format9:16 vertical
ToolSeedance 2.0

06 — Retail promo

Packaging that earns a second look.

A ten-dollar accessory shot like a premium object — particle field, cool key, claim and price landing on beat.

Built to stop a thumb, not to win an award. Different job, different grammar.

Format9:16 vertical
ToolSeedance 2.0
